        }
    }
}

class AndroidReconciliationSignalStore(context: Context) {
    private val preferences = context.getSharedPreferences("reminder_reconciliation.v1", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)

    fun record(reason: ReconciliationReason) {
        val reasons = preferences.getStringSet("reasons", emptySet()).orEmpty().toMutableSet()
        reasons += reason.name
        check(preferences.edit().putStringSet("reasons", reasons).commit())
    }

    fun acknowledge(reason: ReconciliationReason) {
        val reasons = preferences.getStringSet("reasons", emptySet()).orEmpty().toMutableSet()
        reasons -= reason.name
        check(preferences.edit().putStringSet("reasons", reasons).commit())
    }

    fun pending(): Set<ReconciliationReason> {
        val reasons = preferences.getStringSet("reasons", emptySet()).orEmpty()
            .mapNotNullTo(linkedSetOf()) { runCatching { ReconciliationReason.valueOf(it) }.getOrNull() }
        return reasons
    }
}

private fun PhysicalReminder.pendingIntent(context: Context): PendingIntent = PendingIntent.getBroadcast(

        .putExtra(EXTRA_BODY_KEY, bodyKey.name),

)

    val kind: ReminderKind,
    val fireAt: Long,
)

private fun Intent.reminderPayload(): ReminderPayload? {
    val id = getStringExtra(EXTRA_ID)

    val kind = getStringExtra(EXTRA_KIND)?.let { runCatching { ReminderKind.valueOf(it) }.getOrNull() }
    val fireAt = getLongExtra(EXTRA_FIRE_AT, -1)
    if (fireAt < 0) return null
    return if (id != null && title != null && body != null && kind != null) {
        ReminderPayload(id, title, body, kind, fireAt)
    } else null

# Lean independent acceptance

The lean request fixes AppSpec/workspace fingerprints and unavailable host pairs. Read normative AppSpec sources before work.json or implementer summaries. Inventory approved/excluded requirements, ACs, managed operations and gates using the shared canonical helpers. Inspect normative omissions in prose too. Record reviewed Markdown paths once; no heading-by-heading justification for contextual prose.

Inspect every required `(obligation, surface)` pair from `verification_surface_map(app)` in `vibe_protocol.py`. For each verified pair record real production and test anchors, the assertion that proves behavior, and executed check receipts. Inspect receipt tasks and logs; a zero exit code alone, an unrelated assertion, skipped tests or an unconnected preview is insufficient. Check shared fixtures against actual production graph and platform wiring.

Run missing safe checks using `lean-delivery.py <repo> check`. Use `--runner gradle` for Gradle to hold the workspace mutex. Current global receipts may be reused without running the same matrix again. Do not change source/tests to make an audit pass. The launcher persists your final JSON; never create launch evidence yourself.

Return JSON with:

```json
{
  "requestSha256": "actual request file sha256",
  "startedAt": "actual RFC3339 time",
  "completedAt": "actual RFC3339 time",
  "inventory": {"requirementIds": [], "excludedRequirementIds": [], "acceptanceScenarioIds": [], "managedOperationIds": [], "qualityGateIds": []},
  "reviewedSources": ["product.md", "domain.md", "data.md", "design.md", "quality.md", "flows/FLOW-001.md", "screens/SCREEN-001.md"],
  "obligations": [
    {"id": "AC-001", "surface": "component-test", "result": "verified",
     "production": [{"path": "shared/feature/Example.kt", "symbol": "ExampleComponent"}],
     "tests": [{"path": "shared/feature/ExampleTest.kt", "symbol": "saveSurvivesRestart"}],
     "assertion": "Describe the observed production path and actual assertions, including restart.",
     "receiptRefs": [".vibe/receipts/RECEIPT-real-id.json"]}
  ],
  "findings": [],
  "verdict": "PASS"
}
```

Use actual inventory, paths, symbols, times and receipts. Include all pairs, not only the illustration. `result` is `verified`, `gap`, `unavailable` or `not-applicable`. Gaps need reason and actionable findings. Unavailable is only for exact host pairs in the request; inspect the implementation that can be checked locally. Not-applicable is only for inactive conditional external/release gates and must name the condition and why it is inactive. No implicit waivers of repository behavior.

For the independent audit surface of the closure gate, use `result: verified`, `auditEvidence: true` and an assertion explaining the inventory/wiring review; the launcher/validator supplies its own execution proof instead of requiring a recursively pre-existing audit receipt. This exception applies only to a surface named `independent-audit` or `acceptance-audit` or `audit` on a gate, never to product tests.

PASS means all locally available obligations are proven, no local gap or finding remains. GAPS lists known missing behavior/evidence; BLOCKED explains why a reliable assessment is unavailable. Completion flags are computed by the host, not invented by the auditor. For delta review, inspect changed file hashes and consumers, close previous findings with new proof and return a complete current inventory. Request a fresh full audit if scope or independence no longer permits delta review.

# Data

## Local persistence

Use a shared Kotlin Multiplatform database for relational product data, typed Multiplatform Settings for small preferences/privacy caches, and private app storage for imported observation photos. Managers own persistence boundaries; Stores never call database or platform APIs directly.

Expected local records include:

- grow zones and capacity;
- tray-size presets;
- personal recipes and recipe stages;
- grow batches with immutable recipe, tray, substrate, culture, supplier/cultivar/lot, and zone-name snapshots;
- stage events and derived scheduled actions;
- harvest plans and suggestions;
- observations and photo references;
- terminal outcomes and optional actual mass;
- notification preferences and stable scheduled IDs;
- theme preference;
- Crashlytics collection preference;
- one versioned advertising privacy payload containing only the minimal endpoint response, current choice, and matching policy version.

Use stable language-neutral IDs and foreign keys. Do not persist resolved built-in translations.

## Managed operations

`app-spec.json#managedEntities` is authoritative. Important consequences:

- Deleting zones, presets, or recipes does not erase immutable batch snapshots.
- Delete and terminal batch outcomes are different operations.
- Backup archives are immutable external files; create another archive rather than updating one.
- Ad-consent withdrawal is an update, not deletion.
- Crash reporting always has a default-on release preference and is disabled by updating that preference.

## Built-in catalog

Ship catalog content as versioned, deterministic local seed/reference data with stable culture IDs and string-resource keys. Recommended structure:

- `catalogVersion`: a simple monotonic content version;
- `reviewedOn`: content update date;
- culture ID and scientific/common-name resource keys;
- source URL/title metadata;
- stage applicability and duration ranges;
- blackout/weight and presoak flags/ranges;
- metric density input and its source/version;
- substrate/lighting notes as resource keys;
- safety note keys;
- illustration resource name.

Updating the catalog needs no external approval, signature, or attestation. It must change the version/date, preserve IDs where semantics are unchanged, document sources, and pass QG-011. A breaking identity change requires an explicit migration.

## Localized text storage

The complete English key set lives in `shared/compose/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings.xml`; Russian lives in `values-ru/strings.xml`. Catalog seed data and database rows contain only IDs/resource keys. Resolve keys to generated `Res.string.*` accessors at the presentation boundary.

User-authored recipe names, supplier/lot notes, observations, and batch notes are stored verbatim and are not resource strings. Native-only Android/iOS permission and platform text uses native localized resources with English base and Russian addition.

## Backup archive

The full backup is a versioned local archive selected through the platform document provider. It contains:

- a manifest with schema/version and counts;
- all product records and stable relationships;
- app-owned observation photos with integrity metadata;
- user preferences needed to restore product behavior;
- no Crashlytics server data, advertising SDK cache, detected country/IP, advertising ID, or secrets.

Before restore, parse and validate the complete archive, show a localized preview, and require explicit replacement confirmation. Replacement is transactional: stage files and database content, commit both, then rebuild only future reminders. Invalid or unsupported archives leave existing data and files untouched. Restoring the same archive again replaces rather than merges, so it cannot duplicate records.

CSV export contains a localized or documented stable header contract for batch history, culture/recipe identity, relevant dates, outcome, actual mass, and user notes as appropriate. It excludes photographs and does not serve as a restorable backup.

## Remote APIs

### Privacy-region endpoint

Use `GET https://168.222.252.178/v1/privacy/region` exactly as defined by the monetization contract. Send no query parameters or user/install/location identifiers. Accept only strict schema 1 JSON with exact JSON content type, a supported policy version string, and `expiresAt` no more than 72 hours ahead. Reject redirects, non-200 responses, malformed/oversized/non-UTF-8 bodies, unknown schema, stale/overlong expiry, and transport failures.

The endpoint is an accepted shared service. Do not create a backend, alternative service, live qualification, readiness attestation, or endpoint-specific release gate.

### Yandex Ads

Send only the configured ad-unit ID unless a later approved privacy inventory adds something. No product data, notes, schedules, culture choices, photos, user ID, location, or account data enters an ad request. Debug/test uses test IDs; previews and automated tests make no real requests.

### Firebase Crashlytics

Crashlytics is configured separately for Android and iOS release/release-candidate builds. Do not add Firebase Analytics. Do not set a user ID or log user-authored text, crop/recipe selections, schedules, photos, advertising state, or breadcrumbs. Allowed context is limited to app version, platform/build, stack traces, ANR/fatal data, selected technical non-fatals, and reviewed non-PII technical keys.

The release default is collection enabled. The persisted user toggle disables or re-enables future collection according to the platform SDK contract. Local reset does not claim to delete reports already sent to Firebase.

## Offline and cache behavior

- Core database, catalog, photos, plan, history, backup, export, and Settings work offline.
- A valid privacy-region response may be cached only until its accepted expiry, clamped to 72 hours.
- Missing/stale privacy data disables ads for that launch; it does not delay app startup or core screens.
- Crash reports may remain queued by the native SDK contract, but upload never blocks the UI.
- There is no cloud sync, merge policy, login token, or remote product cache.

## Retention and erasure

Product data remains until the user deletes individual records, uses Delete all local data, clears app storage, or uninstalls. Delete all removes database rows, private photos, product/settings state, ad-consent payload, and scheduled reminders, then returns to first run. It explains that previously sent Crashlytics reports and externally saved backup/CSV files are not deleted.

# Design

## Lazyweb evidence and direction

Lazyweb was consulted before screen selection.

Queries:

- `daily task dashboard` — strong adjacent evidence for Today hierarchy: current work first, concise status, stable bottom navigation, meaningful empty state.
- `plant growth tracker` — weak coverage; do not copy gamified “growth garden” or streak patterns.
- `harvest schedule planner` — adjacent planning evidence only; SproutPace uses a domain timeline rather than a generic calendar.
- `crop catalog cards` — weak coverage; use Material feed/grid semantics rather than treating results as validated microgreens patterns.
- Advertising research found no matching measured experiment. The qualitative [Agentic Search](https://www.lazyweb.com/agentic-search/2c55a632-370e-4a01-9e89-a6a5198460e8) supports clearly labeled inline browse/history placement and avoiding blocking promotional modals.

After implementation goldens exist, run first-release Lazyweb review over every primary screen and applicable light/dark/stress state. The post-golden report, not this preliminary search, is the implementation review evidence.

## Product expression

Use a calm botanical Material 3 system:

Brand update approved 2026-09-23: logo 1B-1 and palette A (Forest & Lime).
Light actions use forest green, dark actions use lime with dark-green content;
surface elevations, inverse colors and outlines use botanical neutrals. Native
icons preserve the full-color logo; in-app decorative marks retain semantic tint.
See `../docs/design-review/brand-refresh-20260923.md` for the approved mapping.

- warm neutral surfaces;
- green primary roles;
- restrained soil/gold tertiary accents;
- rounded, shallow-tray silhouettes and organic but readable illustration shapes;
- one hero moment on Today: the most important next action and capacity context;
- no streaks, mascots, confetti loops, diagnostic imagery, or novelty controls.

Prefer M3 Expressive variants when the repository's Compose Multiplatform version provides stable/accepted Android and iOS APIs. Otherwise use the semantically equivalent baseline Material 3 component and record the fallback. Do not custom-draw a missing expressive control merely to imitate its appearance.

## Navigation and adaptive layout

Primary destinations are stable:

1. Today
2. Trays
3. Plan
4. Catalog

Settings is a top-app-bar action, not a fifth primary destination.

| Width | Navigation | Content adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compact `<600dp` | Flexible/baseline navigation bar with icon + label | One pane; details navigate forward; 16dp semantic outer margin |
| Medium `600–839dp` | Collapsed navigation rail | One pane by default; optional supporting pane for Plan conflicts |
| Expanded `840–1199dp` | Collapsed/expanded navigation rail | List-detail for Trays, Catalog, Zones, and presets |
| Large `1200–1599dp` | Expanded navigation rail | Fixed list + flexible detail; Plan may show capacity supporting pane |
| Extra-large `>=1600dp` | Expanded navigation rail | Two panes by default; third pane only for a justified Plan conflict detail |

Each screen has one safe-area owner. Scaffold bars/rails own their corresponding inset; content consumes scaffold padding exactly once. Android predictive back and iOS back behavior map to the same platform-neutral navigation outputs.

## Screen inventory and hierarchy

| Screen | Primary task | Canonical layout | Highest-priority action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SCREEN-001 First run | Understand value or configure first cycle | Supporting pane / compact step flow | Continue setup or browse catalog |
| SCREEN-002 Today | Act on current and overdue work | Feed | Complete/open next action; New batch FAB when appropriate |
| SCREEN-003 Trays | Browse planned, active, and history | List-detail | New batch; open selected batch |
| SCREEN-004 Batch editor | Create/correct a batch | Form/supporting pane | Save/confirm batch |
| SCREEN-005 Batch detail | Understand state and record reality | Supporting pane | Confirm next actual stage |
| SCREEN-006 Plan | Edit cadence and resolve future conflicts | List-detail/supporting pane | Confirm suggestion or resolve conflict |
| SCREEN-007 Catalog | Browse built-in and personal recipes | Feed/grid | Open recipe; Create personal recipe |
| SCREEN-008 Recipe detail/editor | Read or edit recipe and sources | Supporting pane/form | Use recipe or Save personal recipe |
| SCREEN-009 Observation editor | Add/edit dated note and photo | Form | Save observation |
| SCREEN-010 Close batch | Record terminal outcome | Form/dialog on compact | Save outcome |
| SCREEN-011 Settings | Control product preferences/privacy/data | List | Contextual setting action |
| SCREEN-012 Zones | Manage capacity | List-detail | Add zone |
| SCREEN-013 Tray sizes | Manage reusable metric presets | List-detail | Add preset |
| SCREEN-014 Backup and restore | Export, preview, replace | List/supporting pane | Create backup or confirm restore |
| SCREEN-015 Advertising privacy | Make or change applicable consent | Full-screen decision on compact | Accept or decline; neither is visually deceptive |
| SCREEN-016 Notifications | Configure summary and permission recovery | Form/list | Enable/disable or change time |

## Material component map

- App framing: `Scaffold`, flexible/baseline top app bars, flexible/baseline navigation bar, collapsed/expanded navigation rail.
- Collections: standard/expressive lists, cards only where one subject and its actions form a coherent object; grids for catalog at wider sizes.
- Primary creation: one labeled extended FAB on Today/Trays when available; remove rather than disable when context makes it invalid.
- Actions: filled/tonal/outlined/text buttons by prominence; icon buttons only for familiar actions with localized semantics.
- Peer categories: primary tabs for Planned / Active / History within Trays. Tabs never represent sequential setup steps.
- Selection: radio buttons or connected button groups for zone type, tray shape, plan mode, and outcome; switches only for independent immediate settings such as Crashlytics and daily summary.
- Inputs: Material text fields with units/supporting text, date/time pickers with manual entry, and system photo/document pickers.
- Temporary decisions: basic dialog for irreversible delete/reset; bottom/side sheet for compact conflict explanation; persistent supporting pane at expanded widths.
- Feedback: actionable snackbars do not auto-dismiss; dialogs are reserved for decisions, not passive success.
- Progress/loading: show only for real database/file/network work. Core local screens prefer stable content/skeleton boundaries over decorative spinners.

## Today hierarchy

1. Page title and Settings action.
2. Hero next-action surface: action, tray/culture, due state, and one primary completion/open action.
3. Overdue actions.
4. Due today.
5. Next sow/harvest suggestion and capacity warning.
6. Calm empty state when no work exists; never replace it with a streak.

Completing a task provides an undo/review path where semantics permit. State is communicated with text/icon/shape as well as color.

## Stage and capacity presentation

Batch detail uses a vertical stage timeline with actual events, predicted windows, skipped markers, and the next action. Stage illustrations are decorative support and never diagnostic evidence.

Capacity is shown as named zones and occupied/available counts. Future conflicts use warning roles plus explicit text and actions: choose another date, choose/add a zone, change capacity, or retain `needs_resolution`. Actual overflow uses the same language but includes `Temporarily unassigned` so a user can record reality.

## Ads and privacy UI

Allowed slots only:

- SCREEN-007: one clearly labeled inline ad after the fourth culture card.
- SCREEN-003 History tab: one clearly labeled inline ad after the fifth historical record.

At most one ad is visible per eligible screen visit. No app-forced refresh loop is required. Ads are absent from short lists, empty/loading/error states, first run, Today, active batch detail, editors, stage confirmation, completion, planning decisions, settings, permissions, backup, and privacy.

No fill, offline, missing/stale eligibility, declined/unresolved consent, missing ID, SDK error, or iOS no-ID collapses the slot without blocking or leaving a misleading placeholder.

The app-owned protected-region consent screen appears at the first ad-eligible moment only when a fresh endpoint response requires it. It provides accept, decline, and privacy-policy actions with equal clarity. Non-protected responses show no global ad-consent popup or opt-out. Settings exposes withdrawal only while fresh applicability requires consent.

## Theme and tokens

- Default theme policy is system. Settings options are System, Light, and Dark.
- Use semantic color roles and correct `on*` pairings; define a complete accessible warning/success role family if Material roles are insufficient.
- Use Material typography roles and production font glyph coverage for Latin/Cyrillic.
- Use Material spacing tokens based on the 8dp system and minimum 48×48dp targets.
- Prefer tonal surface hierarchy over heavy shadows; keep elevation levels few.
- Use one app-level Material motion scheme. Motion explains selection, expansion, and stage change, never delays task completion.
- Reduced motion replaces translation/morphs with subtle opacity or immediate state changes.

## Typography and text layout

- All bundled copy, errors, accessibility labels, catalog text, and preview text resolves from production EN/RU resources with shared keys.
- User names and notes wrap as data; do not attempt to localize them.
- Titles may use two lines at compact widths before truncation. Critical culture/batch names remain visible; secondary metadata may ellipsize only after its most useful prefix.
- Buttons prefer short sentence-case labels. At 200% font scale, buttons and rows grow/reflow instead of clipping or hiding an action.
- Dates/times use system locale conventions; metric values keep explicit units.
- Never concatenate translated sentence fragments.

## Accessibility

- Meaningful headings and logical reading/focus order.
- Screen-reader action/state names for every control and dynamic status announcement for completed/rescheduled/conflict actions.
- Important state uses at least two cues; capacity, skipped stage, overdue status, selection, and errors cannot rely only on color.
- Minimum 48dp interactive targets, visible keyboard focus, pointer/keyboard alternatives to swipe/drag/long press, and accessible manual date/time input.
- Decorative logos/culture/stage art has null semantics when adjacent copy already carries meaning.
- No time-limited destructive interaction and no auto-dismiss for an actionable snackbar.

## Asset direction

ASSET-001 is the original sprout-over-tray mark. ASSET-016 through ASSET-021 are original vectors. ASSET-022 through ASSET-029 are generated editorial culture covers at the declared size. They must be botanically plausible at microgreen scale, must not include localized text, symptoms, diagnosis claims, logos, or copied public photography, and require visual/content review before delivery.

Standard actions use one Material Symbols Rounded family and the exact resources in `assetRequirements`. Platform launcher/store derivatives follow Android/iOS mask, background, and export rules and are recorded in the delivery manifest.

## Screen state policy

Every screen file decides loading/content/empty/error/offline/permission applicability. General rules:

- Local content never shows a false network-offline error.
- Catalog is bundled and available offline.
- Ads disappear when network/privacy is unavailable.
- Backup/restore shows determinate progress only when measurable and never leaves partial success.
- Permission denial keeps the relevant product action available with explanation and system-settings recovery where appropriate.
- Empty states contain one relevant next action, not marketing filler.

## Preview and golden contract

Every primary screen has deterministic content and applicable empty/error/permission/conflict previews in light and dark. Risk matrix includes:

- EN 100% compact phone;
- RU 200% compact phone using production strings/font;
- expanded-width list-detail layout;
- long user-authored names;
- permission denied;
- offline ad-hidden state;
- capacity conflict/unassigned state;
- destructive confirmation;
- restoration preview/error;
- protected consent and no-consent-needed states.

ComposablePreviewScanner must discover production component-owned preview implementations and generate stable Paparazzi IDs. Record, inspect, approve, then verify goldens. First-release Lazyweb review covers all primary screens after approved goldens.

docs/design-review/production-ui-redesign-20260927.md:47:This review closes the product-design surface, not every external release gate. Publication is not requested in this delivery, so store publication/signing, production Firebase symbolication, production Yandex ad-device validation, and store/privacy disclosure publication are inactive until their required external projects, credentials, policy URL, and explicit publication request exist. package com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.catalog

import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.BuiltInCulture
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.CultureId
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.DurationRange
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.GrowStage
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.LocalizationKey
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.SeedDensity
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.SourceMetadata
import com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.domain.model.StageGuidance
import kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.days
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.hours

object SproutPaceCatalog {
    const val VERSION: Int = 1
    val reviewedOn: LocalDate = LocalDate(2026, 9, 20)

    private val pennState = SourceMetadata(
        url = "https://extension.psu.edu/a-step-by-step-guide-for-growing-microgreens-at-home",
        titleKey = LocalizationKey("source_penn_state_growing_guide"),
        reviewedOn = reviewedOn,
    )
    private val pennStateAbcs = SourceMetadata(
        url = "https://extension.psu.edu/the-abcs-of-microgreens",
        titleKey = LocalizationKey("source_penn_state_abcs"),
        reviewedOn = reviewedOn,
    )

    val cultures: List<BuiltInCulture> = listOf(
        culture("radish", 0.028, soak = null, blackoutDays = 3..4, harvestDays = 7..10),
        culture("broccoli", 0.022, soak = null, blackoutDays = 3..4, harvestDays = 8..12),
        culture("arugula", 0.018, soak = null, blackoutDays = 3..4, harvestDays = 8..12),
        culture("mustard", 0.020, soak = null, blackoutDays = 3..4, harvestDays = 7..10),
        culture("pea", 0.085, soak = 8..12, blackoutDays = 3..5, harvestDays = 10..14),
        culture("sunflower", 0.090, soak = 8..12, blackoutDays = 3..5, harvestDays = 9..13),
        culture("basil", 0.014, soak = null, blackoutDays = 4..6, harvestDays = 14..21),
        culture("garden_cress", 0.018, soak = null, blackoutDays = 2..3, harvestDays = 7..10),
    )

    val cultureIds: Set<CultureId> = cultures.mapTo(linkedSetOf()) { it.id }

    private fun culture(
        id: String,
        density: Double,
        soak: IntRange?,
        blackoutDays: IntRange,
        harvestDays: IntRange,
    ): BuiltInCulture {
        val stageList = buildList {
            soak?.let {
                add(
                    StageGuidance(
                        GrowStage.SOAKING,
                        DurationRange(it.first.hours, it.last.hours),
                        LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_soaking"),
                    ),
                )
            }
            add(StageGuidance(GrowStage.SOWN, DurationRange(0.hours, 0.hours), LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_sowing")))
            add(
                StageGuidance(
                    GrowStage.BLACKOUT_OR_WEIGHT,
                    DurationRange(blackoutDays.first.days, blackoutDays.last.days),
                    LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_blackout"),
                ),
            )
            add(
                StageGuidance(
                    GrowStage.LIGHT_GROWTH,
                    DurationRange(harvestDays.first.days, harvestDays.last.days),
                    LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_light_growth"),
                ),
            )
            add(StageGuidance(GrowStage.READY_FOR_HARVEST, DurationRange(0.hours, 0.hours), LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_harvest")))
        }
        return BuiltInCulture(
            id = CultureId(id),
            nameKey = LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_name"),
            scientificNameKey = LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_scientific_name"),
            illustrationResourceName = "culture_${id}_cover",
            stages = stageList,
            seedDensity = SeedDensity(density, VERSION, pennState),
            substrateNoteKey = LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_substrate_note"),
            lightingNoteKey = LocalizationKey("culture_${id}_lighting_note"),
            safetyNoteKeys = listOf(
                LocalizationKey("safety_untreated_seed"),
                LocalizationKey("safety_clean_container"),
                LocalizationKey("safety_drinking_water"),
                LocalizationKey("safety_drainage"),
                LocalizationKey("safety_avoid_excess_moisture"),
                LocalizationKey("safety_allergy_awareness"),
                LocalizationKey("safety_images_not_diagnostic"),
            ),
            sources = listOf(pennState, pennStateAbcs),
        )
    }
}

      "title": "Repeat persists a batch before the required editor and explicit Save",

        "shared/compose/src/androidUnitTest/kotlin/com/sedsoftware/sproutpace/compose/ProductionLifecycleFlowTest.kt: abandonRepeatAndActualStorageReopenPreserveTerminalHistory dispatches Repeat and asserts two persisted batches, thereby asserting the wrong product behavior."
      ],
      "requiredChange": "Route Repeat to a retained prefilled batch draft. Persist a new identity only on Save; Cancel/Back must leave the original history and batch count unchanged.",
      "verification": "Exercise the production root/router/component with file-backed storage: Repeat leaves one batch, Cancel leaves one, Save creates a distinct planned batch, and reopening preserves the unchanged original history."
    },
    {

        "capacityDecision selects the first light-capable zone; occupancies includes currently occupying assigned batches, not future interval demand or cumulative suggested batches.",
        "shared/domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/sedsoftware/sproutpace/domain/engine/CapacityEngine.kt: Occupancy contains no interval and the date parameter is conflict metadata rather than a temporal overlap calculation.",
        "shared/data/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/sedsoftware/sproutpace/data/RecipeBatchCommandHandler.kt: saveBatch always writes Placement.None and does not retain selected planned-zone intent.",
        "ProductionScreenDataManagerIntegrationTest tests a zero-capacity zone, while PlannerAndSchedulingTest supplies precomputed capacity decisions. Neither detects overlapping future plans."
      ],
      "requiredChange": "Retain planned placement intent separately from actual occupied placement and evaluate stage/date intervals against applicable zones, confirmed plans and other proposed demand. Preserve requested dates and expose explicit resolution when no feasible placement exists.",
      "verification": "Add production-path cases for two overlapping future batches in one place, overlapping suggestions, a full first zone with a free second zone, applicable dark/light demand, and explicit unresolved conflicts without silently changing dates."
    },
